title: Ex 3.5 #11 · 10-digit numbers with no 0 and exactly three 6's
prompt: How many positive 10-digit integers have no digit equal to 0 and exactly three digits equal to 6?
answer_format: A whole number, or an expression for it like 26^4 or binom(10, 3).

mistakes.hint: The seven digits outside the chosen positions can't be 6 either, or the number would have more than three 6's.
Choosing the positions of the 6's is only part of the job: the other seven digits still need values.
The three 6's are identical, so the order in which you pick their positions doesn't matter.

hints: Start with 10 blank positions and decide which three of them hold the 6's.
Each of the other seven positions gets a digit that is neither 0 nor 6.
solution: Choose the 3 positions for the 6's: $\binom{10}{3} = 120$ ways.
Each of the other 7 positions gets one of the 8 digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9: $8^7 = 2{,}097{,}152$ ways.

reference.note: This exact exercise, restated in ProofLab's words. Uses combinations (Section 3.5) and the multiplication principle.
